text:
alex: Heads up — noticed token leakage on the SignalBoard panel for the main cost dashboard. Per-token cost spikes don't match cache hit rate for the last 20m. Anyone else seeing this?

tanya: Yep saw that too. looks like `cache_hits` stayed ~92% but token_cost jumped 3x around 15:12 UTC.

matt: Which route? can you paste the query or trace?

alex: route=/v1/generate user=acme-inc, sample from the edge slice. Quick snippet from the metrics query:```ts
select time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, sum(tokens) as tokens, avg(cache_hit) as cache_hit, sum(cost) as cost
from invocation_metrics
where route = '/v1/generate' and tenant = 'acme-inc'
group by t
order by t desc
limit 20
```

priyanka: Are we sure `cache_hit` here is prefix cache and not KV cache? dashboards mix both sometimes which confuses attribution.

jen: I can repro in staging — there's a lag in the ingest pipeline where cache events come in delayed, so cost shows up first and cache hit updates later. probably a sampling/ordering issue.

alex: that matches: raw logs show token burn event at 15:12 and cache ack at 15:12:40. pipeline reorder.

matt: Is the reorder because of the kafka partitioning? we recently changed partition key to tenant+model for throughput. could cause out-of-order if producers use timestamp-based batching.

priyanka: If it's ingestion order, the dashboard's rolling average & alerting will fire false positives. We need a short-term fix: either switch dashboard to use event-time windowing or mark cache signals as eventual and show a warning badge.

jen: short-term patch: add a UI hint "cache metrics may be delayed up to 60s" and change spike alert threshold to 5m anomaly instead of 1m. I'll open a quick PR.

evan: long-term: fix the ingestion. thoughts: 1) use event_time ordering in materialized view, 2) add a join window when computing per-token cost vs cache, or 3) attach sequence numbers to events.

alex: preference 1 + 3. event_time fixes visualization and seq numbers let us detect reorders. seq numbers also help for rehabbing historical reconciliations.

matt: engineering caveat: event-time windows mean we need watermarking. our streaming infra (flink) supports it but we need to tune allowed lateness. if we set lateness to 60s we avoid most spikes but increase materialization delay.

priyanka: tradeoff: accuracy vs real-timeness. For cost alerts we care more about not alerting incorrectly. For live SLOs we want immediacy. maybe two views: realtime (best-effort) and reconciled (event-time) for billing panels.

alex: agree. console should surface both: "Realtime (estimated)" and "Reconciled (finalized in ~2m)". Ops can triage on Reconciled.

jen: I'll push a tiny UX tweak to show a reconciliation progress bar on the cost card. low-risk.

cost-bot: alert muted for route=/v1/generate for 15m due to known ingest-reorder (ticket #IN-4521).

evan: also let's add a telemetry flag when a reconciliation changes cost > 10% so we can gather stats on how often this happens across tenants/models.

alex: good call. priyanka can you add that to the econ schema? tag as `reconciled_delta_pct` and `reconciled_latency_s` fields.

priyanka: on it. will add schema change + migration notes. will also include a lightweight backfill job to compute reconciled deltas for last 24h.

matt: FYI I'll audit the kafka producer changes and revert partitioning tweak if it's the root cause. posting findings in the thread soon.

alex: thanks all — action list: jen UI hint + progress bar PR, priyanka schema + backfill, matt audit + revert if needed, evan design seq + watermark plan. I'll follow up on IN-4521 and keep everyone posted. :thumbsup:
